symptoms: Vigorous, uniform tillering
Erect and deep green leaf blades without lesions
Clean, unblemished leaf sheaths at the water line
Panicles emerging uniformly, filling out completely without chaffiness or grain discoloration
prevention: Basal nutrient management including split doses of Nitrogen, total Phosphorus and Potassium applied before planting
Essential micronutrient additions, specifically Zinc and Calcium Silicate to physically fortify cell walls
Use of biofertilizers like Azospirillum and Phosphobacteria to enhance seedling vigor and root mass
monitoringAdvice: Regular checks of the water level
farmerFriendlyExplanation: A healthy rice crop has lots of strong stems (tillers), erect green leaves with no spots, clean stems near the water line, and rice heads that fill out fully without empty grains or discoloration. In Telugu, it is called స్వస్థ వరి (Swastha vari) and in Hindi as स्वस्थ धान (Swasth dhaan).

symptoms: Entire seedlings wilt, roll up, turn a grayish-green, and die completely (Kresek Phase / Seedling Wilt)
Water-soaked streaks near leaf tips and margins (Leaf Blight Phase)
Streaks enlarging, coalescing, and turning a distinctive yellow-white with highly characteristic wavy margins
Entire leaf drying up and dying
Milky bacterial ooze drops on young lesions early in the morning
Crusty, amber-colored beads on the leaf surface (dried ooze)
earlySymptoms: Seedling wilting and rolling up, turning grayish-green (Kresek phase)
Water-soaked streaks near leaf tips and margins in mature plants
advancedSymptoms: Streaks enlarging, coalescing, and turning yellow-white with wavy margins, leading to the entire leaf drying and dying
Milky bacterial ooze drops drying into crusty, amber-colored beads on leaf surfaces
causes: Pathogen entry through hydathodes (natural pores) or microscopic wounds

low: Stop applying Urea immediately (as nitrogen feeds the bacteria)
medium: Temporarily drain the field to stop water-borne spread
high: Foliar spray of Copper Hydroxide to halt bacterial entry

organicTreatments: Use Pseudomonas fluorescens seed treatment @ 10g/kg seed
Use seedling root dip @ 2.5 kg/ha in 100 L water prior to transplanting

chemicalTreatments.sprayInterval: Administered at 30 and 45 days after planting

prevention: Seed treatment and seedling root dip with Pseudomonas fluorescens
Strictly avoid excessive or late nitrogen top-dressing
Maintain proper field water levels and drain temporarily if symptoms appear
monitoringAdvice: Check seedlings 1-3 weeks after transplanting for wilting/rolling leaves
Inspect mature leaves for early morning milky ooze drops or dried amber beads
Check leaf tips and margins for yellow-white streaks with wavy margins
farmerFriendlyExplanation: A severe bacterial infection that enters through cuts in the leaves. It starts at the tips, turning leaf edges yellow and wavy, eventually killing the whole leaf. It spreads rapidly through irrigation water and rain. The farmer must immediately stop applying Urea, drain the field temporarily, and spray Copper Hydroxide. Known as జీవాణు పత్తీ జులసా (Jiwanu patti jhulasa) in Hindi and బాక్టీరియా ఆకు ఎండు తెగులు (Bacteria aaku endu tegulu) in Telugu.

symptoms: Small, numerous, cylindrical or oval spots on leaves
Advanced lesions that are dark brown with a highly distinct, bright yellow halo (resembling sesame seeds)
Spots coalescing, drying up the leaf entirely
Scorched, burned appearance of the nursery or field from a distance
Black spots on the glumes (grains)
Failure of seed germination
Reduced weight and quality of the harvest
earlySymptoms: Small, numerous, cylindrical or oval spots on the leaves
advancedSymptoms: Dark brown spots with bright yellow halos, resembling sesame seeds scattered across leaves
Spots coalescing, causing leaves to dry up completely and giving the field a scorched appearance
causes: Poor soil fertility and nutrient deficiencies

spreadConditions.season: Associated with poor soil fertility (potassium/nutrient deficiency) and moisture stress

low: Ensure the field has adequate fertilizer, especially potassium
Correct any water shortages to relieve moisture stress
medium: Foliar spray of undiluted cow urine as an organic alternative
high: Foliar spray of Mancozeb upon symptom appearance to stop spot progression

organicTreatments: 100% cow urine foliar spray to suppress the pathogen
prevention: Integrate nutrient management with seed treatment
Hot water treatment (53 C) of seeds for 10-12 mins
Seed soak with Captan or Thiram
Ensure adequate soil fertility and moisture management
monitoringAdvice: Check leaves from seedling to milky grain stage for cylindrical spots
farmerFriendlyExplanation: A fungus that creates small, dark brown, sesame-seed-like spots with yellow rings around them. It thrives when the soil is poor in nutrients or water-stressed, making the field look scorched and turning the rice grains black. The immediate action is to ensure the field has adequate fertilizer (especially potassium) and water, and spray Mancozeb or undiluted cow urine. Known as భూరా ధబ్బా (Bhura dhabba) in Hindi and ఆకుపై గోధుమ రంగు మచ్చల తెగులు (Aakupai godhuma rangu machala tegulu) in Telugu.

symptoms: Spindle-shaped (eye-shaped) lesions with grey centers and dark brown margins on foliage (Leaf Blast)
Black lesions on the stem nodes (Nodal Blast)
Girdling of stem nodes, causing stems to break easily
Rotting and blackening of the peduncle/neck (Neck Blast)
Blanking (empty, white, erect panicles) (early neck infection)
Partial, chalky grain filling (late neck infection)
Complete blockage of nutrient and water flow to the grain
earlySymptoms: Highly distinctive spindle-shaped (eye-shaped) lesions with grey centers and dark brown margins on the leaves
advancedSymptoms: Black lesions on stem nodes, girdling them and causing breakage
Infected neck rots, turns black, leading to empty white panicles (blanking) or partial chalky grains

medium: Foliar spray of Carbendazim or Edifenphos if 2-5% of leaf area shows spindle spots
high: Spray Tricyclazole immediately upon seeing eye-shaped spots on leaves
Apply a mandatory preventative spray of Tricyclazole right before grain heads emerge to save yield from neck blast

Systemic fungicide spray right before panicle emergence

farmerFriendlyExplanation: A devastating fungus that first creates eye-shaped spots on the leaves. Its most dangerous form attacks the neck of the stalk just below the grain head, rotting it completely so the grains end up empty and white. Spray Tricyclazole immediately upon seeing leaf spots, and apply a mandatory preventative spray just before grain heads emerge to protect the crop. Locally known as జొంకా రోగ్ / అగ్గి తెగులు (Jhonka rog) in Hindi and అగ్గి తెగులు (Aggi tegulu) in Telugu.
